### 2.1 System Pointers (Zero Page)

| Name | Address | Meaning |
|------|----------|----------|
| **TXTTAB** | `$002B–002C` | Start of BASIC text (default `$0801`) |
| **VARTAB** | `$002D–002E` | Start of variable table |
| **ARYTAB** | `$002F–0030` | Start of array storage |
| **STREND** | `$0031–0032` | End of arrays (+1) |
| **FRETOP** | `$0033–0034` | Bottom of string storage |
| **MEMSIZ** | `$0037–0038` | Highest BASIC RAM address |

Variables grow upward from `TXTTAB`; strings grow downward from `MEMSIZ`.  
`ARYTAB` always follows `VARTAB`; defining new scalars after arrays shifts array memory upward by 7 bytes per variable.

## Compact Workflows

| Need | Preferred mechanism | Minimal sequence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Evaluate expression | `FRMNUM`/`FRMEVL` | Set `TXTPTR` to first char, `JSR $AD8A` or `JSR $AD9E`, handle BASIC errors. |
| Numeric result as text | `FOUT` | FAC1 ready, `JSR $BDDD`, copy A/Y string immediately. |
| Parse byte/address syntax | `GETBYT`/`GETADR`/`GETNUM` | Use BASIC-compatible expression text and controlled `TXTPTR`. |
| Read/write numeric scalar | `PTRGET` + `MOVFM`/`MOVMF` | Set `TXTPTR` to var name; use returned `VARPNT`. |
| Install tokenized program | Raw write + `LNKPRG` + `CLR` | Write at `TXTTAB`, final next pointer `$0000`, `JSR $A533`, `JSR $A65E`. |
| Execute BASIC statement | Dynamic keyboard or normal interpreter | Avoid direct statement entries unless runtime/error context is controlled. |
| Reserve high RAM | Lower `MEMSIZ`, then `CLR` | Update `$37/$38`, `JSR $A65E`; keep ML/sprites above new top. |

## 1. Raster IRQ and IRQ chains
Setup with KERNAL off (`$01=$35`; hardware vectors used):
```
        sei
        lda #$35
        sta $01
        lda #$7f          ; CIA IRQ sources off
        sta $dc0d
        sta $dd0d
        lda $dc0d         ; acknowledge pending
        lda $dd0d
        lda #<nmi
        sta $fffa
        lda #>nmi
        sta $fffb
        lda #<irq_top
        sta $fffe
        lda #>irq_top
        sta $ffff
        lda #$1b          ; bit 7 = raster line bit 8 = 0
        sta $d011
        lda #50
        sta $d012
        lda #$01          ; VIC raster IRQ on (enable last)
        sta $d01a
        lda #$ff
        sta $d019
        cli
main:   jmp main          ; main loop; never fall through into nmi
nmi:    rti
irq_top: pha
        txa
        pha
        tya
        pha
        lda #$ff          ; ack all VIC sources
        sta $d019
        ; ... work ...
        lda #<irq_next    ; chain: next vector and line
        sta $fffe
        lda #>irq_next
        sta $ffff
        lda #200
        sta $d012
        pla
        tay
        pla
        tax
        pla
        rti
```
- With the KERNAL on, use the vector `$0314/$0315` and exit with `jmp $ea31` (clock, cursor, keyboard scan) or `jmp $ea81` (registers and `RTI` only).
- Lines above 255: set `$D011` bit 7 for that entry (the 9th raster bit). Always rewrite `$D011` with bit 7 matching the next line.
- Chain rules: entries sorted by line; handler worst-case time shorter than the gap to the next entry; if the next line has already passed when you program `$D012`, run the next handler directly instead of waiting a whole frame; acknowledge `$D019` first; save `$01` if the main loop changes it. NMI must have a vector (RESTORE key).

## 2. Sprite multiplexing (more than 8 sprites)
Algorithm (standard, from Cadaver's write-up):
1. Keep a list of virtual sprites (24 in Cadaver's and Corescape's multiplexers): x (9-bit), y, frame, colour. Sort by Y each frame, ascending.
2. Map sorted sprite k to hardware sprite `k mod 8` (rotation).
3. A hardware sprite with Y coordinate Y is displayed in lines Y+1 to Y+21 and its DMA ends in line Y+22; a new Y starts a new display only while the DMA is off (Bauer 3.8.1 rules 2, 4, 7). So virtual sprite k reuses hardware sprite `k mod 8` only if `Y(k) >= Y(k-8) + 22`, and the raster IRQ at line `Y(k-8) + 22` rewrites its Y, X, pointer and colour. Otherwise the sprite is not shown this frame (flicker policy: drop the lowest priority one).
4. After the last sprite, park unused hardware sprites at Y = 255 (or clear `$D015`); precompute `$D010` bit masks per sprite.
5. Reject sprites outside the visible area and if more than 8 would sit on one raster line (hardware limit); the 9th simply does not appear.
- Sorting: insertion sort over a persistent order table (Y order changes little per frame), in zero page. Zones instead of sorting: fixed horizontal bands each owning a fixed sprite subset (HUD, boss); cheapest, limited layout.
- Placement code (64tass; entered from the raster IRQ after the acknowledge, frame start sets `slot = 0`; a sprite closer than 21 lines below its hardware predecessor is shown late, so drop it in the sort stage):
```
; Sorted tables, ascending sy, written by the main loop into the back copy and swapped (eor #MAX flag):
; sy,sx(low 8 bits),sp(pointer),sc(colour),msb(0 or the $D010 bit of the hardware sprite when x>=256),
; hw2 (slot -> 2*(slot and 7)), clr (slot -> $FF minus that $D010 bit), 32 bytes each; zero page: slot, nspr, nline.

records.name: data/gamedev/techniques.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/gamedev/techniques.md#2. Sprite multiplexing (more than 8 sprites) -->
mux:    ldy slot
place:  ldx hw2,y         ; X = 2 * hardware sprite
        lda sy,y
        sta $d001,x
        lda sx,y
        sta $d000,x
        lda $d010
        and clr,y
        ora msb,y
        sta $d010
        txa
        lsr
        tax               ; X = hardware sprite
        lda sp,y
        sta $07f8,x
        lda sc,y
        sta $d027,x
        iny
        cpy nspr
        bcs done          ; all placed: next IRQ is the frame-start entry
        cpy #8
        bcc place         ; the first 8 sprites are placed back to back
        lda sy-8,y        ; the hardware sprite used 8 slots ago ends 21 lines below its Y
        clc
        adc #22
        sta nline
        lda $d012
        clc
        adc #3
        bcs place         ; raster is near the bottom
        cmp nline
        bcs place         ; line passed or too close to arm an IRQ: place now
        sty slot
        lda nline
        sta $d012         ; (Y+22 < 256 assumed: clamp sprites that reuse a slot to Y < 234)
        rts
done:   rts
```
- Cost counted from the c64ref cycle table, tables not crossing a page: 74 cycles per sprite placed back to back, 115 for a sprite after which the routine arms the next IRQ, plus 3 for `ldy slot` and the caller's IRQ entry and exit. 24 virtual sprites need at most 24 x 115 = 2,760 cycles per frame.
- A collision bit names the hardware sprite, so with multiplexing it cannot tell which virtual sprite collided: test collisions in software on the virtual list.
- Hardware priority: `$D01B` per sprite (behind/in front of foreground chars), `$D01C` multicolour, `$D017/$D01D` expand (expanded sprites occupy more lines: use their real height in rule 3).

## 3. Smooth scrolling
- Hardware fine scroll: `$D016` bits 0-2 (X), `$D011` bits 0-2 (Y). Use 38-column mode (`$D016` bit 3 = 0) and 24-row mode (`$D011` bit 3 = 0) so new data enters under the border.
- Horizontal loop: fine X goes 7 down to 0 (scrolling left); when it wraps, shift screen RAM left by one character and set X back to 7 (or reverse). Keep the new column prepared in advance from the tile map (a 2x2 or 4x4 character metatile per map cell).
- Fine-scroll step, once per frame from the top IRQ (content moves left one pixel per frame; `shift_left` copies screen RAM one column left into the other screen and writes the new column, spread over the 8 steps):
```
scroll: lda $d016
        and #$07
        beq wrap            ; fine X reached 0
        dec $d016           ; 7..1: one pixel left
        rts
wrap:   lda $d016
        ora #$07            ; back to 7
        sta $d016
        jmp shift_left      ; then flip $D018 to the other screen at the next top IRQ
```
- Double-buffer screen RAM (two screens at `$C000`/`$C400`, flip `$D018` and sprite pointers on the wrap). Spread the shift over the 8 fine steps (for example 3 rows per frame) so no frame overruns. An unrolled `lda abs,x / sta abs,x` copy costs 9 cycles per byte (4 + 5; 1 more when the load crosses a page): 24 rows (960 bytes) cost 8,640 cycles.
- Colour RAM `$D800` exists once and cannot be double-buffered. Options: (a) give the whole scrolling area one colour RAM value and take the other colours from `$D021-$D023` in multicolour mode, so colour RAM never moves; (b) copy it row by row just behind the raster beam; (c) shift it in the same split steps; (d) bitmap mode, where screen RAM holds two of the colours.

## 6. Music and sound effects
- PSID files (GoatTracker and SID-Wizard export them) carry load, init and play addresses (`c64://sound/sid/file-format`). Load the player at its load address; call `init` once with the song number minus one in A (`$00` = song 1); call `play` once per frame from the raster IRQ at a fixed line. A play address of `$0000` means the tune installs its own interrupt: do not call it (`SID_file_format.txt` "initAddress", "playAddress").
- Reserve the player's zero page and RAM range in the memory map first. A player at `$A000-$BFFF` needs LORAM=0: `$01` = `$36`/`$35`/`$34`.
- Speed: a tune written for PAL runs 19.4 % fast on NTSC (59.826 / 50.125 frames per second). On NTSC skip one call in six (49.86 calls per second, 0.5 % slow):
```
        dec tick
        bpl +
        lda #5
        sta tick
        bne skip          ; skip this frame's play call
+       jsr play          ; (tick counts 5..0, so one in six frames is skipped)
skip:
```
  A song whose PSID `speed` bit is 1 expects `play` from a CIA 1 timer A interrupt at the rate its `init` sets (60 Hz default); call it from that interrupt, not from the raster IRQ (`SID_file_format.txt` "speed").
- SFX on one SID: dedicate voice 3. After `jsr play` each frame, if an effect is active write its frequency/pulse/ADSR/control to `$D40E-$D414` from a table (one step per frame); at its end write control with gate off and the player retakes the voice at its next note. A priority byte stops a weak effect cutting a strong one. Or use a player with built-in SFX.
- Volume `$D418` is shared and also holds filter mode: write it once per frame in one place.
- MODERN, several SIDs: the address map, the `.cfg` that places the chips, detection and mixing are in `c64://ultimate/multisid`; read it before writing to any address above `$D41F`. Without that setup play one SID at `$D400`. Digitised audio from the REU: `c64://ultimate/reu`.
**Seen in:** Tetris C64 (`LoadSid`, init/play from frame code), Tony (player in `$A000-$BFFF`), Oscar64 `sidfx` sound effects.

## 7. Random numbers
```
rnd:    lda seed          ; 8-bit Galois LFSR, period 255; seed must not be 0
        asl
        bcc +
        eor #$1d
+       sta seed
        rts
```
- Seed from something unpredictable at the first fire press: `$D012` XOR a free-running CIA timer low byte, or the frame counter when the player pressed a key.
- SID noise as a hardware source: voice 3 frequency `$D40E/$D40F = $FFFF`, control `$D412 = $80` (noise, gate off), read `$D41B` (upper 8 bits of oscillator 3). Voice 3 then cannot play music; set `$D418` bit 7 to disconnect it from the output (Mapping `$D41B`).

## 8. PAL / NTSC timing
- Detect once at start. Quick: KERNAL byte `$02A6` (1 = PAL, 0 = NTSC), set by the KERNAL at reset (Mapping `$02A6`). From the line count: PAL 6569 has 312 lines (highest line `$137`, so `$D012` reaches `$37` with bit 8 set); NTSC 6567R8 263 lines (`$106`), 6567R56A 262 lines (`$105`) (Bauer 3.4).
```
detect: lda $d011
        bpl detect        ; wait until raster line >= 256
chk:    lda $d012
        cmp #$10
        bcs is_pal        ; saw a line number >= 272
        bit $d011
        bmi chk           ; still above line 255
        lda #0            ; wrapped to line 0: NTSC
        rts
is_pal: lda #1
        rts
```
- Consequences: frame budget (architecture), music speed (above), bottom-border IRQ lines, sprite Y ranges, colours, game speed (frame counters scaled by a speed table).
- MODERN: the Ultimate setting `System Mode` takes `PAL`, `NTSC`, `PAL-60`, `NTSC-50`, `PAL-60/L`, `NTSC-50/L` (`u64/u64_config.cc:278`; measured): detect at run time, never from the product name. `c64://ultimate/hardware`.

3. Speed probe: counts passes of a 14-cycle loop through one line without bad lines, interrupts off. It returned 4 at 1 MHz in VICE 3.10. On Ultimate 64 Elite it returned 4 in 20 of 20 runs at 1 MHz, 8 or 9 at 2 MHz, 17 or 18 at 4 MHz and 196 or 197 at 48 MHz (Ultimate 64 Elite, firmware 3.15a, 2026-11-20). On a C64 Ultimate (measured on C64 Ultimate, firmware 1.2.1, 2026-11-20) it returned 4, 8 or 9, 17 or 18, 201 at 48 MHz and `$FF` (saturated) at 64 MHz (80 samples per speed). The values at 32 and 48 MHz differ between the models (U64 142 / 196-197, C64U 144 / 201), so do not compare against fixed numbers above 4 MHz; compare against the 1 MHz result. More than 4 means a faster CPU. It does not give MHz: time a longer loop against CIA2 (`c64://ultimate/hardware`, "Measuring speed").
```
speed:  lda #$fa
-       cmp $d012           ; line $FA: below the last badline ($F7)
        bne -
w:      cmp $d012           ; wait until the line changes: line $FB starts
        beq w
        tax
        inx                 ; X = $FB
        lda #0
        sta cnt             ; cnt: one zero-page byte
l:      inc cnt
        beq full            ; wrapped: saturate
        cpx $d012
        beq l
        lda cnt
        rts
full:   lda #$ff
        rts
```
4. UCI: `lda $df1d / and #$7f / cmp #$49`: the command interface returns `$C9`, or `$49` while its IRQ is active, only when `Command Interface` is enabled (`fpga/io/command_interface/vhdl_source/command_protocol.vhd:99`). REU: presence, size probe and level load in `c64://ultimate/reu`. SIDs: `c64://ultimate/multisid`.

## 11. Bitmap and multicolour modes
Mode bits: `$D011` bit 5 BMM, `$D016` bit 4 MCM, `$D011` bit 6 ECM = 0 (Bauer 3.7.3).
| Mode | BMM, MCM | Pixels | Colour of bit pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| Multicolour text | 0, 1 | 4x8 per character whose colour RAM bit 3 is 1; others stay hires in colours 0-7 | `00` `$D021`, `01` `$D022`, `10` `$D023`, `11` colour RAM bits 0-2 |
| Standard bitmap | 1, 0 | 320x200, colours per 8x8 cell | `0` screen byte bits 0-3, `1` screen byte bits 4-7 |
| Multicolour bitmap | 1, 1 | 160x200, pixels twice as wide | `00` `$D021`, `01` screen bits 4-7, `10` screen bits 0-3, `11` colour RAM bits 0-3 |
- Memory: the bitmap is 8 KB at bank offset `$0000` or `$2000` (`$D018` bit 3); the screen matrix (cell colours) at `$D018` bits 4-7 x `$400`. In banks 0 and 2 the character ROM image at offset `$1000-$1FFF` hides that RAM, so the bitmap goes to `$2000` there.
- Setup, bank 0, colours at `$0400`, bitmap at `$2000`:
```
        lda #$3b          ; $D011: BMM, DEN, RSEL, YSCROLL 3 (RST8 0)
        sta $d011
        lda #$18          ; $D016: MCM, CSEL (use #$08 for hires bitmap)
        sta $d016
        lda #$18          ; $D018: screen $0400 (1 x $400), bitmap $2000 (bit 3)
        sta $d018
```
- Layout: 8 consecutive bytes form one 8x8 cell, cells run left to right, 40 per row (320 bytes per cell row). Hires byte for (x, y): `base + 40 * (y AND 248) + (y AND 7) + (x AND 504)`, bit `7 - (x AND 7)` (leftmost pixel = bit 7). Multicolour (x = 0-159): byte `base + 40 * (y AND 248) + (y AND 7) + 2 * (x AND 252)`, bit pair `(3 - (x AND 3)) * 2` upwards.
- Clear the bitmap (8000 bytes) and set the 1000 screen bytes (and colour RAM for multicolour) before turning the mode on, or blank the screen (`$D011` bit 4 = 0) while you do.

<!-- Source: data/graphics/sprite-charset-best-practices.md#Character Definition Format -->
### Character Definition Format

Each character uses 8 bytes (8 rows × 8 pixels):

```text
Byte 0: Row 0 bitmap (MSB = leftmost pixel)
Byte 1: Row 1 bitmap
...
Byte 7: Row 7 bitmap
```

Example: 'A' character

```text
00111100  ($3C) - Row 0
01100110  ($66) - Row 1
01100110  ($66) - Row 2
01111110  ($7E) - Row 3
01100110  ($66) - Row 4
01100110  ($66) - Row 5
01100110  ($66) - Row 6
00000000  ($00) - Row 7
```

### Charset Memory Alignment

Custom charsets must be aligned to 2KB boundaries:

- `$2000` (8192) - VIC bank 0, offset $2000
- `$2800` (10240) - VIC bank 0, offset $2800
- `$3000` (12288) - VIC bank 0, offset $3000
- `$3800` (14336) - VIC bank 0, offset $3800

In bank 0 the offset equals the address.

## Character ROM

The **Character ROM** (*chargen*) for the C64 is **4 KB at $D000–$DFFF (53248–57343)**, consisting of **two 2 KB sets** (each 256×8-byte glyphs):

- **Set 1 (uppercase/graphics):** $D000–$D7FF (53248–55295), 256 entries
- **Set 2 (lowercase/uppercase):** $D800–$DFFF (55296–57343), 256 entries

**Screen codes** index glyphs; **PETSCII codes** are logical character codes used by BASIC/KERNAL. Screen memory at **$0400–$07E7** stores screen codes that the **VIC-II** uses to fetch 8-byte bitmaps from the active character set.

## Graphics Modes (ECM/BMM/MCM)

Graphics mode is selected by the following bits in $d011 and $d016:

- `ECM` (bit 6 of $d011): Extended Colour Mode.
- `BMM` (bit 5 of $d011): Bit Map Mode.
- `MCM` (bit 4 of $d016): Multi Colour Mode.

| Mode | Bits (ECM/BMM/MCM) | Memory interpretation | Pixel output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standard text | 0/0/0 | `c`: char code + colour nybble; `g`: CB bits + RC | 8x8 pixels; bit 1 uses `c[11:8]`, bit 0 uses B0C ($d021$). |
| Multicolour text | 0/0/1 | `c[11]` selects multi flag | Flag 0: standard text; flag 1: 4x8 pixels, 00->B0C, 01->B1C, 10->B2C, 11->`c[10:8]`. |
| Standard bitmap | 0/1/0 | `c`: foreground/background nybbles; `g`: bitmap byte | 8x8 pixels; bit 0 -> `c[3:0]`, bit 1 -> `c[7:4]`. |
| Multicolour bitmap | 0/1/1 | `c`: colours for 01/10/11 | 4x8 pixels; 00->B0C, 01->`c[7:4]`, 10->`c[3:0]`, 11->`c[11:8]`. |
| ECM text | 1/0/0 | Upper char bits select B0C..B3C (char set reduced to 64) | Foreground uses `c[11:8]`; background chosen via `c[7:6]`. |
| Invalid text | 1/0/1 | Same addressing as ECM multi; outputs black | Useful for collision tricks; no visible pixels. |
| Invalid bitmap 1 | 1/1/0 | Bitmap with A9/A10 forced low | Displays black; repeats sections; collisions still occur. |
| Invalid bitmap 2 | 1/1/1 | Multicolour bitmap with A9/A10 forced low | Black output; collisions possible; 4x8 grouping. |
| Idle state | any (when sequencer idle) | `g` fetch at $3fff/$39ff, video matrix treated as zero | Outputs backgrounds per mode (typically B0C or black). |

## CIA #2 Registers (`$DD00–$DD0F`) — IEC/User Port/RS‑232/VIC Bank/NMI

| Address | Decimal | Name | Function / Bits (compact) |
|:-------:|:-------:|:-----|:---------------------------|
| `$DD00` | 56576 | **PRA** | **IEC** + **VIC bank** + RS‑232 TXD. **b7** DATA IN, **b6** CLOCK IN, **b5** DATA OUT, **b4** CLOCK OUT, **b3** ATN OUT (bus lines active‑low via drivers); **b2** RS‑232 TXD (user M); **b1..b0** VIC 16 KiB bank: `00=$C000–FFFF`, `01=$8000–BFFF`, `10=$4000–7FFF`, `11=$0000–3FFF` (power‑on `11`). |
| `$DD01` | 56577 | **PRB** | **User Port/RS‑232** lines (TTL). **b7** DSR (L), **b6** CTS (K), **b5** User‑J, **b4** DCD (H), **b3** RI (F), **b2** DTR (E), **b1** RTS (D), **b0** RXD (C). **Also:** PB7/PB6 timer outputs when enabled. |
| `$DD02` | 56578 | **DDRA** | Port A direction. Default `$3F` (b6–b7 in). |
| `$DD03` | 56579 | **DDRB** | Port B direction. Default `$00`; RS‑232 may set b1–b2 out when opened. |
| `$DD04` | 56580 | **TALO** | Timer A low (R counter / W latch low). |
| `$DD05` | 56581 | **TAHI** | Timer A high (R counter / W latch high). |
| `$DD06` | 56582 | **TBLO** | Timer B low. |
| `$DD07` | 56583 | **TBHI** | Timer B high. |
| `$DD08` | 56584 | **TOD10TH** | TOD tenths BCD. (OS typically unused here.) |
| `$DD09` | 56585 | **TODSEC** | TOD seconds BCD. |
| `$DD0A` | 56586 | **TODMIN** | TOD minutes BCD. |
| `$DD0B` | 56587 | **TODHR** | TOD hours BCD + AM/PM (b7). |
| `$DD0C` | 56588 | **SDR** | Serial shift data (rarely used by OS; available via user port SP2/CNT2). |
| `$DD0D` | 56589 | **ICR** | As CIA1, but flags drive **/NMI**. **b4**=FLAG (user‑port pin B). |
| `$DD0E` | 56590 | **CRA** | As CIA1 `$DC0E`. |
| `$DD0F` | 56591 | **CRB** | As CIA1 `$DC0F`. |

**Notes (CIA2):** Provides **IEC** master control (ATN/CLOCK/DATA), **User Port** digital I/O and RS‑232 signals, and **VIC bank** selection via `PRA[1:0]`. `/PC2` (handshake) pulses low for one cycle after **PRB** access—available on user port for external strobing.

| Control | $D404 | $D40B | $D412 | **7..0 = NOISE PULSE SAW TRI TEST RING SYNC GATE** |
| AD | $D405 | $D40C | $D413 | Attack/Decay nibbles |
| SR | $D406 | $D40D | $D414 | Sustain/Release nibbles |

**Global:**

| Function | Address | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| Cutoff LO | $D415 | Bits 0-2 = low 3 bits of filter cutoff |
| Cutoff HI | $D416 | High 8 bits of filter cutoff |
| Res/Routing | $D417 | 7..4 = resonance (0–15); 3..0 = route Ext,V3,V2,V1 into filter |
| Mode/Volume | $D418 | 0..3 = master vol (0–15); 4..6 = LP/BP/HP; 7 = CH3 off |
| Read-backs | $D419–$D41C | POTX, POTY, OSC3, ENV3 |

<!-- Source: data/sound/sidwave.md#Instrument pulse and filter tables -->
### Instrument pulse and filter tables

Both tables restart on each note start and advance once per player call, including at
`speed` greater than 1. A table can be a list of steps or a mapping with `steps`
and its own zero-based `loop` index. For lists, an instrument-level `loop`
applies to each list on that instrument. Without a loop, the last value holds
after the final step finishes, including when the last step was an `add`. The
compiled player supports up to 255 pulse steps and 255 filter steps across its
instrument variants.

`pulsetable` supplies the voice's pulse width via `$D402 + 7v` and
`$D403 + 7v` (`v` is 0–2). A `set` takes a fraction in `(0, 1]` or an
integer from 1 to 4094. Values up to and including 1 are interpreted as fractions,
scaled by 4095, rounded, and clamped to 1–4094. An `add` applies a signed
delta from −2048 to 2047 on each of its `frames` calls (1–255), clamping the
result to 1–4094. A `set` lasts one call by default and can also specify
`frames`. The table takes priority over `pwm_sweep`. If the first step is an
`add`, it starts from the note's `pulse_width` (default 2048).

`filtertable` sets the cutoff to an integer in 0–2047 with `cutoff`, or
changes it on every call with an `add` delta from −2048 to 2047, clamped to
0–2047. Each step has `frames` in 1–255 (default 1). Optional `resonance`
(0–15) and `type` carry forward when omitted. A note starts with cutoff 0,
resonance 8, and `lowpass` before its first step runs. The filter types are
`lowpass`, `bandpass`, `highpass`, `lowpass+highpass`, `bandpass+highpass`,
and `all`. The player puts cutoff bits 0–2 in `$D415` and bits 3–10 in
`$D416`, resonance and routing in `$D417`, and type in `$D418` while
preserving the current master volume.

| Turbo Control | Value the firmware writes to the core (`setCpuSpeed`, `software/u64/u64_config.cc:1696-1708`) | Effect for a program |
|---|---|---|
| `Off` | turbo enable `$00`, speed `$80` (index 0) | 1 MHz; `$D030`/`$D031` read `$FF` |
| `Manual` | `$00` | `CPU Speed` applies; `$D031` reads `$FF`; `$D07A`/`$D07B` have no effect (measured U64) |
| `U64 Turbo Registers` (C64U: `C64U Turbo Registers`) | `$01` | `$D031`, `$D07A`, `$D07B` change the speed. After a reset `$D031` reads `$00` and the CPU runs at 1 MHz; `CPU Speed` is only the speed that a write to `$D07B` selects (measured U64 3.15a) (measured on C64 Ultimate, firmware 1.2.1, 2026-11-20). Switching from `Manual` without a reset keeps the last `$D031` value |
| `TurboEnable Bit` | `$05` | as the registers mode, plus `$D030` bit 0 (0 = 1 MHz, 1 = selected speed) |

In `Manual` mode `$D031` reads `$FF` for the CPU and `CPU Speed` applies from 4.17 s after the reset; a reset in `Manual` mode does not clear a `$D031` value written earlier in a registers mode (the value reappears when a registers mode is selected without a reset) (measured on C64 Ultimate, firmware 1.2.1, 2026-11-20).

`SuperCPU Detect (D0BC)` = `Enabled` adds `$02` to the turbo enable value in every mode except `Off`.

## I/O area `$DE00-$DFFF`

| Range | Device |
|---|---|
| `$DF00-$DF0A` | REU (c64://ultimate/reu). Reads of `$DF0B-$DF17` return `$FF` (`fpga/cart_slot/vhdl_source/reu.vhd:429-487`). No Ultimate product has the extended REU registers `$DF0C-$DF0F`: every public top level and the U64, U64 Elite II and C64 Ultimate images build the REU without them; measured on U64 core 1.50, reads return `$FF` and writes are ignored. |
| `$DF1B-$DF1F` | UCI (`$DF1C-$DF1F`; `$DF1B` = IEC device number); at `$DE1B-$DE1F` under an EasyFlash `.crt`; c64://ultimate/uci |
| `$DF20-$DFFF` | Ultimate Audio sampler, when `Map Ultimate Audio $DF20-DFFF` = `Enabled` (default `Disabled`) |
| `$DE00`, `$DF00` or `$DF80` | ACIA 6551 (SwiftLink), item `ACIA (6551) Mapping`: `Off`, `DE00/IRQ`, `DE00/NMI`, `DF00/IRQ`, `DF00/NMI`, `DF80/IRQ`, `DF80/NMI` (default `Off`, `software/io/acia/modem.cc:46,69`) |
| `$DE00-$DFE0` | optional SID placements |

A loaded `.crt` decides which Ultimate devices stay on (`software/io/c64/c64.h:243-258`, `c64_crt.cc:468-648`, `c64.cc:1358-1430`):

| CRT class | Switched off | Forced on |
|---|---|---|
| `PROHIBIT_DEXX` | ACIA at `$DE00` | - |
| `PROHIBIT_DFXX` | ACIA at `$DF00`, REU, UCI at `$DF1C`, sampler | - |
| `PROHIBIT_IO` | all of the above | - |
| EasyFlash subtype 1 | ACIA, sampler | UCI at `$DE1C`; REU follows its setting |
| EasyFlash other subtypes | ACIA, REU, sampler | UCI at `$DE1C` |
| C128 std-IO subtype 1 / Final Cartridge III subtype 1 | ACIA, sampler | C128 subtype 1: UCI at `$DF1C` |
| C128 std-IO subtype 2 | ACIA at `$DF00`/`$DF80`, sampler | UCI at `$DF1C` |

"Forced on" applies even when `Command Interface` is `Disabled`. A CRT game uses the REU, sampler or ACIA only if its type leaves them on.
- The ACIA's Turbo232 register sets the modem baud rate, not the CPU speed.
- Real-time clock: UCI DOS `GET_TIME`; there are no memory-mapped RTC registers.

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/multisid.md#Address rules -->
## Address rules

- Four decoders (Socket 1, Socket 2, UltiSID 1, UltiSID 2), each a 32-byte window. Legal addresses: `Unmapped`, `$D400`-`$D7E0` and `$DE00`-`$DFE0` in steps of `$20` (49 labels). Keep SIDs out of `$DE00-$DFFF` (REU, UCI).
- `UltiSID Range Split` (shared by both UltiSIDs): `Off`, `1/2 (A5)`, `1/2 (A6)`, `1/2 (A7)`, `1/2 (A8)`, `1/4 (A5,A6)`, `1/4 (A5,A8)`, `1/4 (A7,A8)`. The split bits are cleared from the base, then every combination is a part. With UltiSID 1 `$D400` and 2 `$D420`: A6 gives `$D400,$D440`/`$D420,$D460`; A7 `$D400,$D480`/`$D420,$D4A0`; A8 `$D400,$D500`/`$D420,$D520`; (A7,A8) all eight. Splits that contain A5 make UltiSID 2 overlap UltiSID 1 at these addresses: do not use.
- `Ext DualSID Range Split` (sockets): `Off`, `A5` to `A9`; the bit is removed from both socket decoders and drives the chip's address-select line. A9 is the only choice that keeps the 10-SID map free of overlaps.
- Two decoders at one address both receive the write (no priority).
- `Auto Address Mirroring`: after the split bits are removed, an address bit A5-A9 becomes "don't care" if all mapped decoders agree on it, so the map repeats. The 10-SID map repeats at plus `$200`; with both sockets `Unmapped` it repeats at plus `$40` and `$200`. `Disabled` leaves exactly the listed windows (device).
- Access only mapped windows: never probe candidate addresses in `$D400-$D7FF`, and never REST `readmem` the whole I/O area while a split map is active. The effect of an access to an undecoded address is listed under Not verified.
- The firmware writes `$D41F`, `$D43F` and `$D51F` when the C64 returns from the menu (`restore_io`, `software/io/c64/c64.cc:1119-1121`): keep `$D400`, `$D420` and `$D500` decoded (the 10-SID map does).

## Recipe: 3 independent SIDs, sockets empty, SID 2 hard right

1. Host or install time: UCI enabled (`C64 and Cartridge Settings / Command Interface=Enabled`).
2. Write this `.cfg` (to `/Temp/g.cfg` via DOS target, or ship it) and send `04 50 /Temp/g.cfg` (LOAD_CONFIG below):
   `[SID Addressing]` `Auto Address Mirroring=Disabled`, `UltiSID Range Split=1/4 (A7,A8)`, `UltiSID 1 Address=$D400`, `UltiSID 2 Address=$D420`, `SID Socket 1 Address=Unmapped`, `SID Socket 2 Address=Unmapped`, `Ext DualSID Range Split=Off`; `[Audio Mixer]` `Pan UltiSID 1=Left 5`, `Pan UltiSID 2=Right 5`.
3. Eight windows are live (map under Owner configurations). Use SID A `$D400`, SID B `$D500` (UltiSID 1, left), SID C `$D420` (UltiSID 2, hard right); never touch unmapped addresses. This split keeps `$D500` decoded for the freezer.
4. Per SID write registers `$00-$18` at its base (voice 1 `$00-$06`, voice 2 `$07-$0D`, voice 3 `$0E-$14`, filter `$15-$17`, `$18` = volume/filter mode). Set `$D418` of each window separately.
5. Verify with the ENV3 test (Detection) on the three windows; on failure play everything on `$D400`.
Pan is per UltiSID, not per part: parts of one UltiSID cannot be panned apart. To pan SID 2 hard right at run time, send a `.cfg` with only `[Audio Mixer]` `Pan UltiSID 2=Right 5` (only listed items change).

## Recipes (assemble with ca65 and 64tass; the first one ran in VICE 3.10 x64sc with `-reu -reusize 128`)

Load a level from the REU into `$4000` (8192 bytes at REU offset `$010000`): write every register first, `$DF01` last.
```
load_level:
        php
        sei
        lda #$00
        sta $DF02         ; C64 address lo
        lda #$40
        sta $DF03         ; C64 address hi: $4000
        lda #$00
        sta $DF04         ; REU address lo
        sta $DF05         ; REU address mid
        sta $DF07         ; length lo
        sta $DF09         ; no REU interrupt
        sta $DF0A         ; both addresses count up
        lda #$01
        sta $DF06         ; REU bank (64 KB units): offset $010000
        lda #$20
        sta $DF08         ; length hi: $2000 bytes
        lda #$91          ; fetch, execute now, no autoload
        sta $DF01         ; MUST be the last register write
        nop
        nop
        plp
        rts
```
For several levels keep one table row per level (REU lo/mid/bank, length lo/hi, indexed by level number) and load `$DF04-$DF08` with `lda tab,x`. The shipped data must not cross a 512 KB boundary and must be at most 64 KB per call (length 0 = 64 KB). Stash is `$90`, swap `$92`, verify `$93`.

<!-- Source: data/ultimate/reu.md#Recipes (assemble with ca65 and 64tass; the first one ran in VICE 3.10 x64sc with `-reu -reusize 128`) -->
Detect an enabled REU (carry set = present; REU byte 0 is restored). A disabled REU does not answer, so this is also the "enabled" check. For the size see "Size detection".
```
reu_present:
        lda #$91
        jsr one           ; tmp = REU[0]
        lda tmp
        sta orig
        eor #$a5
        sta tmp
        lda #$90
        jsr one           ; REU[0] = orig xor $a5
        lda orig
        sta tmp           ; a missing REU leaves tmp = orig, which cannot pass the test
        lda #$91
        jsr one           ; tmp = REU[0] again
        lda tmp
        eor #$a5
        cmp orig          ; equal = the byte came back from REU memory
        php
        lda orig
        sta tmp
        lda #$90
        jsr one           ; restore REU[0]
        plp
        beq yes
        clc
        rts
yes:    sec
        rts
one:    php               ; 1-byte DMA between zero-page byte tmp and REU offset 0
        sei
        ldx #tmp          ; tmp, orig: two free zero-page bytes
        stx $DF02
        ldx #0
        stx $DF03
        stx $DF04
        stx $DF05
        stx $DF06
        stx $DF08
        stx $DF09
        stx $DF0A
        inx
        stx $DF07
        sta $DF01         ; A = command
        nop
        nop
        plp
        rts
```
- In C compilers (Oscar64 reordered stores to constant I/O addresses once) write the register sequence as one inline-assembly block, and re-read the first byte of a fetched buffer through a volatile pointer.

## Display model

- 384x256 pixels = 192 "byte columns" x 256 rows. Column c holds pixel x = 2c in the low nybble and x = 2c+1 in the high nybble, row = offset inside the column (column-major, 256 bytes per column, 49,152 bytes). Same as Upic `.upic` files.
- Pixel address: `col_base(x >> 1) + y`; even x = low nybble mask `$0F`, odd x = high nybble mask `$F0`.
- The buffer is ordinary C64 RAM (default `$1000-$CFFF`). Common layout: first 8 columns relocated to `$E000` (under KERNAL, needs `$01 = $35`), the rest at `$1800 + (c-8)*256`, generated renderer page-aligned at `$E800` up. Resident code and data then fit in `$0800-$17FF` (4 KB) and the RAM above the renderer; large programs use REU overlays.
- A bare 49,152-byte bitmap or v1.3 `.upic` file (256-byte header "Upic1.3" + `$AE`, size fields, text, 48-byte palette at `$D0`, bitmap at `$100`) holds pictures; older converters write a separate `.pal`.
- There is no framebuffer register, blitter or double buffer. Pixels are written by CPU stores, REU DMA or UCI DMA loads into the columns. A second 48 KB buffer does not fit in RAM.
- Palette: pixel values are VIC colour indices 0-15 written to `$D020`; their RGB comes from the Ultimate palette (UCI `04 51-54`; `04 53` set and `04 54` reset of the palette verified on Ultimate 64 Elite, firmware 3.15a, 2026-11-20; the Upic program itself was not run on it). A palette change recolours the whole display at once with no pixel redraw.

# SID Quick Reference (for RAG)

See `data/sound/sid-spec.md` for the full guide. This stub ensures the RAG index includes SID guidance.

- Base address: $D400
- Voice control: $D404/$D40B/$D412 (bits: NOISE PULSE SAW TRI TEST RING SYNC GATE)
- Play note: set FREQ LO/HI, PW LO/HI, AD, SR; set CTRL with waveform|GATE
- Stop note: clear GATE bit in CTRL
- Volume/filter: $D418 (bits 0..3 volume, 4..6 LP/BP/HP)
- Filter cutoff: $D415/$D416 (11 bits)
- Useful effects: arpeggio (rewrite FREQ), vibrato (modulate FREQ), PWM (modulate PW), filter sweeps ($D415/$D416)
